column8: Wed 25 Nov: third read of the same four MSCI levels as Q85 and NUMBERS 9; already in the register, no new fact. Print nothing new.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e/aha 9: three calendars on the verified levels; -42.7% and -44.2% are in NUMBERS 9; corrects Q85-028 (41-42%) and NUMBERS 8x's old -42.1%/-40.6%; say more than 40%, never about 42%. -40.90% needs a NUMBERS line before it is printed.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: peak to low -48.4% on month-ends, so the meetings sat near the low; Keel arithmetic on read levels, needs a NUMBERS entry if printed.
Wed 25 Nov: already says 9.8% was a splice and 16.7% on price alone; this row only confirms. NUMBERS 9 still has to replace the register's about 10%.
Wed 25 Nov: corrects Q85-028 and AHA row 9 (56-57% a splice) with 53.8% or 49.1%; Keel arithmetic, needs a NUMBERS entry before printed.
Wed 25 Nov: sources check and Table 3 row 7: DGBAS CSV route read at source; closes Q85-024's January 2003 gap. Citation only, no prose.
Wed 25 Nov: Jan 2003 to Dec 2004 +18.4% already held; only the building-construction sub-index (+18.35%) is new and adds nothing.
Wed 25 Nov: 27.2% US$ from EXTAUS already held in Q85-026; the 7.46% stronger NT$ is the only addition.
Wed 25 Nov: window sensitivity (+17.9%, +19.6%, 28.0%) already in Q85-024 and Q85-026; cost-peak +22.7% is kept in row 15.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: one calendar per sentence, -44.2% with Jan 2003 to Dec 2004, or -42.7% with Jan 2003 to Jan 2005; the tree l.373-376 mixes them, so it must be fixed.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e/Table 3 row 7: the rise was a burst (11.6% in one quarter), why the answer is money kept back; new beside Q66-037 and Q131-037. DGBAS figures read at source, Keel arithmetic; needs a NUMBERS entry.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: steel was the engine, rebar +37.8% in three months; deepens Q131-017 (different window). Needs a NUMBERS entry for 71.0% and 43.9%.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: burst came from world steel, so a Taiwan-only watch would not see it; CRS and BLS read in excerpt only, so a second look at page and quote before it is cited.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: corrects the tree's followed by; the rise began in 2002 and overlapped the slump by about a year. Say most of the rise came after the meetings.
Wed 25 Nov: 3b/Table 3 row 7: the US$ figure depends on the end month (22.7% to 28.0%); the 10% watch is a trigger, not a size. Extends Q85-026.
Wed 25 Nov: $31,324, $2,642 and $10,145 are Keel arithmetic on 8q pots, in no NUMBERS line; needs a NUMBERS entry (8q/8x) and the replay pot is smaller. Related Q85-027 and Q85-030.
Wed 25 Nov: re-derivation of NUMBERS 8x(d) four episodes and 20 of 406 windows; same figures as Q210-008, no new fact.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e: only one of the four episodes followed a share fall; never cite four times as the aha's frequency. Corrects the tree's use of the four episodes and Q10e-022 partly; 1991-93 leans on a US stand-in (S 4). Needs a NUMBERS entry.
Wed 25 Nov: US shares (OECD) stand in for world shares before 1991-93, so probably is all it can say; world figure unverified. Use only as a footnote in the card, not prose.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e aha 9: 20 meetings months after a 30% slump in three runs, US$ cost up 12.2%-29.4%; new, closes the tendency question as dated events. Overlapping windows, say two events, never a rate; needs a NUMBERS entry.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e aha 9: two slumps, two engines (steel 2003-04, Taiwan dollar 2009-11); new beside Q131-031 and 8q's meetings 2009. Needs a NUMBERS entry for the runs' medians and 22.3%.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: median two-year US$ rise 3.0% over all windows against 27.4/23.7/12.7 after slumps; tied to Q210-025's wide band, so two dated events, never a tendency. Needs a NUMBERS entry.
Wed 25 Nov: record only: correlation -0.32 on about 12 separate spans, band includes zero (Q210-025); never printed, never a tendency. Hard to say in one sentence.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: big rises came by two routes, after a slump and after a boom (2006-08); refines Q66's U-shape and Q10e-022. Overlapping windows; needs a NUMBERS entry.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e: on Laura's January calendar only Jan 2003 followed a 30% slump; the $16,900 need (14.7% of $115,000) is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS, so add it or drop it; a dated fact, never 1 in 25.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e claim (d): HKMA's link since 17 Oct 1983 makes a Hong Kong tender price in effect a US$ price; cites HKMA at source.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e claim (d): Hong Kong after 2008, shares -26.5% then tender prices +17.9%, the outside case the brief wanted; tender (selling) index, not a cost index, so say so. Extends Q66-035.
Wed 25 Nov: the three January purchases (2006-08) overlap and are one slump, not three cases; say so before using, and keep the +17.9% single case.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e/Table 3 row 7: HK tender prices fell 29.8% then rose 43.2%, so the falling cost in the crash year is no comfort; completes Q66-035, whose first half it is.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e claim (d) KILL: 1973-74 then 1974-75 is not a then-case, the burst came with the slump (materials +29.2%, shares -45.0%); corrects store rows Q66-035, Q6c-001/003/005, Q85-007/016 that carried it as a case. Keep as the kill record.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: HK tender prices fell 35.7% after 1974, so building got cheaper; supports the kill in row 30. HK$ floated then, so not a US$ price; low value.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: 1975-76 US materials +15.6% against CPI +11.7% was inflation-paced, not a burst; supports the kill, low value.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e: the 2004 steel burst reached US construction materials (+15.2%), so not an independent case; supports row 13 only.
Wed 25 Nov: 3e/Table 3 row 7: the same world shock landed differently (HK -2.6%, US materials +0.5% in 2009-10), so watch Taiwan's own index and dollar, not a world average.

Wed 25 Nov: 3e spine row 9: the truest single-episode form (-44% to Jan 2003, +18% NT$ and +27% US$, most in one quarter of 2004); one calendar, so it pairs with row 10. Rests on NUMBERS 9 and rows 7-8, 11; most of it holds (11.6 of 18.4 points).

Wed 25 Nov: 3e aha 9: the count of two dated events, steel then the Taiwan dollar, plus Hong Kong; keep can, never tends to. Careful: the 2010 run's median was only 12.7%, and HK 2009-12 is three overlapping purchases, not three cases. Needs a NUMBERS entry.
